newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures widen losses on production data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures widen losses on production data.

text.p: U.S. debt futures widened opening losses, as the U.S. industrial production data eradicated faint talk that the U.S. Federal Reserve would not raise rates in May, traders and analysts said.
U.S. industrial production rose 0.9 percent, against average trade estimates for a rise of 0.6 percent and February's upwardly revised increase of 0.6 percent.
Capacity utilization rose to 84.1 percent, its highest rate in two years, and much higher than average trade forecasts for 83.6 percent. February's use rate was also upwardly revised to 83.6 percent.
June T-bonds inched through support at 107-13/32 before the numbers were released, but quickened its pace to the downside after the headline numbers rolled across the tape.

The contract initially found bids at 107-04/32, but proceeded to fall through the 107-00 level, a trader said. Support is at 106-28/32, the level where the contract rebounded from after the U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) was released on Monday, one bond futures analyst said.
Further support is at the seven-month low of 106-12/32, with key support pegged at the 105-18/32 area which currently corresponds to a long bond yield of 7.00 percent, he said.

Meanwhile, September Eurodollars tested 93.66, the lower end of its trading range. Support is at 93.64, which has been the contract's daily low for the last three trading sessions. Some analysts also pegged support at 93.62, which is the 61.8-percent Fibonacci retracement level.
Open interest for September Eurodollars rose more than 12,000 contracts on Tuesday, erasing some beliefs that short-covering was widespread during pit trade.
"On rebounds you would expect shorts to get out of positions, but possibly any short-covering was offset with new short positions," one Eurodollar futures trader said.
Another floor trader noted that total open interest was still relatively low in the face of the Federal Reserve's tightening mode.
"There are still a lot of people staying on the sidelines," he said.

Bond traders said volume was heavier on the downside, rather than on the market's brief rally after the U.S. housing starts data. Starts fell to a rate of 1.425 million units, compared to average trade estimates of 1.46 million and against February's downwardly revised rate of 1.522 million units.

At 1023 CDT/1523 GMT, June T-bonds were 15/32 lower at 107-05/32, notes were off 09/32 at 105-16/32, September T-bills were up 0.025 to 94.32, and September Eurodollars were off 0.03 to 93.68. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
